description.narrative: Basrah Gas Company (BGC) is an Iraqi midstream natural gas company created to gather, treat and process associated gas flared at oil fields in southern Iraq. BGC commenced operations in May 2013 and operates compressor stations, various gas processing plants, a pipeline network and a storage and marine terminal for export. It produces dry gas and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for sale into the Iraqi gas grid, and some LPG and condensate for export. The proposed investment entails the rehabilitation and upgrade of the storage terminal at Umm Qasr port (Project) and the refinancing of the outstanding loan committed by IFC in 2021, which financed the upgrade of the Basrah Natural Gas Liquids (BNGL) facility. Both the Project and BNGL form part of Phase II of BGCs multi-phase expansion program, which is expected to increase raw gas processing capacity from 1 billion standard cubic feet per day (bscfd) to 1.4 bscfd and LPG processing capacity from 4,000 tonnes per day (tpd) to 11,000 tpd.

The Project is expected to significantly reduce gas flaring, which will increase domestic gas production and have significant positive environmental impacts by avoiding greenhouse gas emissions. The Project is also expected to generate additional revenues to the Government of Iraq by increasing exports through the expansion of LPG storage and transportation capacity at the Umm Qasr terminal, through tax revenue collection, and through the Governments ownership shares in BGC through South Gas Company. The Project is expected to improve the resilience of Iraq's energy sector by reducing reliance on more polluting energy sources, such as high-sulfur fuel oil or crude oil, for power generation and by reducing reliance on gas imports.
